417.description:
On Thursday, October 14, 2021, at 10:00 a.m. EDT, the Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests, and Public Lands (NPFPL) will hold a virtual, fully remote legislative hearing on the following bills:

H.R. 149 (Rep. Donald Norcross), To designate the Peter J. McGuire Memorial and Peter J. McGuire Gravesite located in Pennsauken, New Jersey, as a National Historic Landmark, and for other purposes. Peter J. McGuire Labor Day Landmark Act. 
H.R. 250 (Rep. Ann Kirkpatrick), To authorize the Secretary of the Interior to establish the January 8th National Memorial in Tucson, Arizona, as an affiliated area of the National Park System, and for other purposes. January 8th National Memorial Act. 
H.R. 3197 (Rep. Mike Johnson), To direct the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the City of Eunice, Louisiana, certain Federal land in Louisiana, and for other purposes. Save the Liberty Theatre Act of 2021.
H.R. 3531 (Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton), To authorize the Women Who Worked on the Home Front Foundation to establish a commemorative work in the District of Columbia and its environs, and for other purposes. Women Who Worked on the Home Front World War II Memorial Act. 
H.R. 4009 (Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton), To authorize the Georgetown African American Historic Landmark Project and Tour to establish a commemorative work in the District of Columbia and its environs, and for other purposes. Georgetown Waterfront Enslaved Voyages Memorial Act.
H.R. 4380 (Rep. Veronica Escobar), To designate the El Paso Community Healing Garden National Memorial, and for other purposes. 
H.R. 4454 (Rep. Al Green), To establish a process for the Board on Geographic Names to review and revise offensive names of Federal land units, to create an advisory committee to recommend Federal land unit names to be reviewed by the Board, and for other purposes. Reconciliation in Place Names Act. 
H.R. 4648 (Rep. Mike Johnson), To modify the boundary of the Cane River Creole National Historical Park in the State of Louisiana, and for other purposes. Cane River Creole National Historical Park Boundary Modification Act. 
H.R. 4706 (Rep. Tony Gonzales), To establish the Blackwell School National Historic Site in Marfa, Texas, and for other purposes. Blackwell School National Historic Site Act.

488.title: Bishop Calls on House to Pass Bill Mitigating COVID Impacts to Navajo
488.description: On October 1, 2020, Ranking Member Bishop requested unanimous consent for immediate consideration in the House of S. 886, the Indian Water Rights Settlement Extension Act. S. 886, which passed the Senate with bipartisan support on June 4, includes Bishop's legislation, H.R. 644 - Navajo Utah Water Rights Settlement Act.  In order to address COVID-19, the public must be able to take basic preventative measures such as hand washing. The lack of running water for more than 40 percent of the population on the Navajo Reservation has made the residents of the reservation disproportionately susceptible to the virus.  The House has an opportunity to take immediate action to mitigate future COVID-19 outbreaks and address the drinking water crisis on the Navajo Reservation by passing S. 886. Unfortunately, Democrats rejected Bishop's request to act on the bill.

489.title: Republicans Reject Democrats’ Attempt to Politicize Puerto Rico Sovereignty Amid Pandemic
489.description: During a hearing before the House Committee on Natural Resources Committee, Republicans pushed backed against Democrats’ attempts to undermine Puerto Rico’s sovereignty amid the COVID-19 pandemic and politicize the Commonwealth’s economic recovery. Republican Members further excoriated Democrats for sidelining elected voices of the minority and favoring political messaging pursuits over the needs of the American people.

490.title: Rep. Rob Bishop Urges Democrats to Fix Our National Parks
490.description:
Today, Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah) spoke on the House floor in opposition to H.R. 2546, a package of bills titled Protecting Americas Wilderness Act. These bills represent the Democrats’ failed public lands management agenda and would singlehandedly result in catastrophic wildfire seasons, contain opposition from local stakeholders and counties, and hinder military readiness. 

Bishop highlighted H.R. 1225, the Restore Our Parks and Public Lands Act, which would address the deferred maintenance backlog that currently stands at $16 billion for all public land, including a $12 billion backlog within our National Park System. These backlogs are wreaking havoc on agency budgets and jeopardizing the safety and quality of visitors’ enjoyment to National Parks. H.R. 1225 has garnered immense bipartisan support and passed Committee by a vote of 36-2.

491.title: Rep. Rob Bishop Slams Democrats on Subpoena Power Grab
491.description: Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah) slammed Democrats at a scheduled Committee markup on their intent to grant themselves unilateral subpoena authority. This authorized resolution would wipe out input of Minority members, take Committee decision making behind closed doors, and provide unchecked authority over private citizens and agencies.

492.title: Spotlight Series: Episode 2 w/ Rep. Kevin Hern (Holiday Special)
492.description: This week, we sat down with U.S. Representative Kevin Hern (R-Oklahoma) for a holiday themed episode two of the Spotlight Series. We talked about his future plans in the Natural Resources realm as we head into 2020, and what his favorite stocking stuffer happens to be. There is loads of Big Macs and candy themed content above, with a musical guest appearance from Kurt Russell as Santa Claus himself. From everyone at @NatResources, we wish you a Merry Christmas!

493.title: Rep. Tom McClintock Introduces Western Water Legislation
493.description: Today, Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah), Rep. Tom McClintock (R-Calif.), Republican Leader Kevin McCarthy (R-Calif.) and Republican colleagues introduced legislation designed to reform water policy in the west. H.R. 5217 the Water Optimization for the West Act (WOW), puts common-sense principles into policy and ensures that storage projects are funded, streamlined, and operated efficiently. The WOW Act prioritizes that we can prepare for dry years in times of abundance and that the greening of the West in the 20th century isn’t followed by an aridification at the hands of shortsighted policy.

494.title: Rep. Bishop Opening Statement on Partisan Natural Resources Democrats
494.description: Today, Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah) and Committee Republicans motioned to adjourn from a scheduled Committee markup when Democrats failed to show up. Once again, a Chairman Grijalva markup was stripped of legislation capable of becoming law and instead, stuffed with partisan bills going nowhere. Much like the House as a whole, this Committee has been the victim of shameless virtue-signaling where politics have taken precedent over good policy.

495.title: Spotlight Series: Episode 1 w/ Rep. Bruce Westerman
495.description: Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-Ark.) gets in the spotlight, answers questions on his priorities on the Natural Resources Committee, favorite tree, and more.

496.title: Rep. Rob Bishop Dismisses Push for Partisan Federal Land Legislation
496.description: Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah) testified at the house Committee on Rules regarding legislation scheduled this week for consideration on the House floor. H.R. 2182, 1373, and 823 would stifle rural economic development, weaken our national security by ensuring foreign countries supply our critical mineral demands, and adversely affect American jobs.

497.title: Rep. Rob Bishop Pushes Back On Democrat Anti-Mining Agenda
497.description: Today, Ranking Republican of the House Committee on Natural Resources Rob Bishop (R-Utah) addressed the short comings of the Hardrock Leasing and Reclamation Act (H.R. 2579) being considered during the scheduled Full Committee Markup. The legislation would have serious ramifications for critical mineral production and domestic supply. In order to develop modern weapons systems, solar panels, wind turbines, batteries for electric vehicles, and smart phones, the U.S. must prioritize domestic investment in our hardrock industry. Failing to will result in outsourcing extraction and production to foreign countries with dubious standards to safeguard their workers and environment, while making us susceptible to oversea adversaries like China and Russia.

498.title: Bishop Bemoans Democrat Hypocrisy Stalling National Park Backlog Solution
498.description:
Today, Ranking Republican Rob Bishop (R-Utah) reproached democrats on their blatant hypocrisy at the Subcommittee on Water Oceans and Wildlife legislative hearing. Since meeting democrat requirements for a floor vote, leadership in the House Committee on Natural Resources have neglected to advance the overwhelmingly bipartisan maintenance backlog legislation. Democrats have now pivoted, standing behind a belief that the solution to repair our National Parks needs a pay-for before it can be considered on the House floor.  

The park backlog is supported by a bipartisan coalition of 318 members of Congress.

963.description:
“EPA is the one ultimately taking responsibility for this and DOI will tell us whether mistakes were made at the site, or whether there was any misjudgment," EPA Administrator Gina McCarthy. 

After repeatedly assuring the Committees that the pending DOI report would answer such questions about EPA’s potential negligence or wrongdoing, Administrator McCarthy testified that to ensure the report would get to the bottom of things, EPA was “going with the agencies that have significant expertise, the Department of the Interior, the Army Corps of Engineers. 

Secretary Jewell went on to directly contradict Administrator McCarthy’s previous testimony that DOI was responsible for investigating whether EPA had acted negligently or criminally leading up to the spill. Concerning DOI’s role, Secretary Jewell stated: “My understanding is the EPA is doing a thorough investigation with people that are trained to do that. The people that did our report are trained engineers, and they delivered exactly what we agreed to do with the EPA, sir." She reiterated that DOI “did exactly what the agreement with the EPA was, in terms of providing a technical review.”

1166.title: President Obama on Supporting Energy Infrastructure
1166.description:
Flashback: “We will soon lay down thousands of miles of power lines that can carry new energy to cities and towns across this country.” -President Obama, 2009

Fast forward: By 2012, only 15 power lines were completed. Most recently, the White House strongly opposed H.R. 2358, the Electricity Reliability and Forest Protection Act, which corrects the federal inconsistency and indecision that ties the hands of our local providers. As bill sponsor Congressman Ryan Zinke stated, “Currently, if a tree falls on a power line that is on federal land, utility crews must go through regulatory back flips just to remove it…It really should not take an act of Congress to remove a tree.” He continued, stating our co-ops “deserve far better, as do all Americans who need reliable electric service to keep their lights on.” 
Does that sound like supporting energy infrastructure to you?

1167.title: President Obama on the Success Government-Backed Green Energy Companies
1167.description:
Flashback: “You can see the results of last year's investments in clean energy -– in the North Carolina company that will create 1,200 jobs nationwide helping to make advanced batteries; or in the California business that will put a thousand people to work making solar panels.” -President Obama, 2010

Fast forward: Enerdel, the North Carolina battery company, filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2012 after receiving a $118 million U.S. Energy Department grant. Solyndra, the California business, received a $535 million loan guarantee from the government before going bankrupt in 2011. The company also spent nearly $1.8 million lobbying the government prior to receiving the loan guarantee.

1168.title: President Obama on Decreasing Bureaucracy
1168.description:
Flashback: “In the coming months, my administration will develop a proposal to merge, consolidate, and reorganize the federal government in a way that best serves the goal of a more competitive America.” -President Obama, 2011

Fast Forward: The Obama administration is less efficient than ever. Two separate Government Accountability Office (GAO) reports released in 2015 highlight problems created by the federal government’s heavy-handed regulatory climate. The first report titled, "Indian Energy Development: Poor Management by BIA Has Hindered Energy Development on Indian Lands," focuses on the vast inadequacies of the federal government in regards to Native American energy development. The second report, “BLM Has Limited Assurance That Wind and Solar Projects Are Adequately Bonded” discusses the Bureau of Land Management (BLM)’s chronic mismanagement of its bonding program for renewable energy projects.

1169.title: President Obama on Creating Jobs through American Energy
1169.description:
Flashback: "One of the biggest factors in bringing more jobs back is our commitment to American energy. The all-of-the-above energy strategy I announced a few years ago is working, and today, America is closer to energy independence than we’ve been in decades." -President Obama, 2014

Fast Forward: The Obama administration continues to aggressively pursue industries like mining and job creators like power plants by introducing economy-killing regulations. One of the best and most recent examples of this is the EPA Clean Power Plan which was announced just this past August. Regulations like these hurt low income families by increasing the cost of energy, while decreasing opportunities for Americans to get to work.

1170.title: President Obama on Fostering Energy Production and Independence
1170.description:
Flashback: “My administration will keep cutting red tape and speeding up new oil and gas permits.” -President Obama, 2013

Fast Forward: The Obama Administration has closed off millions of acres of public lands and waters to American energy production, offered the fewest offshore lease sales in the history of the program, and caused energy production on federal lands to significantly decline. Meanwhile, the private sector and individual states—not President Obama and the federal government—can take credit for America’s recent increase in oil and natural gas production.

1171.title: President Obama on Increased Offshore Leases
1171.description:
Flashback: “Tonight, I’m directing my administration to open more than 75 percent of our potential offshore oil and gas resources.” -President Obama, 2012

Fast Forward: This was one of his most misleading claims. The truth is that 75% of our offshore resources were never open. When he made this statement, only 38 million acres—or a mere 2.16% - of 1.76 billion acres in the U.S. Outer Continental Shelf were actually leased for energy development. Since 2012, The Obama administration has taken a number of actions to restrict future offshore drilling in the Arctic Ocean. For example, in October 2015, the Interior Department canceled two lease sales for Arctic drilling rights and denied two oil companies’ requests to extend the time on leases that they already held. 1312.title: Bipartisan support for H.R. 2647, The Resilient Federal Forests Act
1312.description:
H.R. 2647, the “Resilient Federal Forests Act of 2015,” is a comprehensive bill aimed at expediting and improving forest management activities in federal forests. Following passage of H.R. 2647 on June 11, 2015 in the Committee on Natural Resources, the House Agriculture Committee on June 17, 2015, approved H.R. 2647.  The bipartisan bill addresses disastrous consequences of catastrophic wildfire, insect and disease infestations, and other threats to our nation’s forests. It also seeks to return resilience to overgrown, fire-prone forested lands.
